## 2. Every owner intervention, its mechanism, its knobs, its failure behaviour

The eight items are `run-summary.md` §"Owner interventions this time".

### Item 1 — Capacity: limits restated, ~90 dead sessions, ten hand cap edits

**Mechanism: an AIMD capacity controller with per-endpoint health.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Component** | `local/bin/capacity_controller.py`, supervised by `results/telemetry/owner-tools/capacityd.sh` (60 s tick), installed by the versioned installer (§7). |
| **Inputs** | `run-mode.json` (ceiling, `external_reserved`, `enabled`, endpoint); `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` rows carrying `failure_class` and `endpoint` (see Item 7 below and §2/L-series); `accounts/<account>/` live markers. |
| **Knob file** | `local/capacity-policy.json` (committed): per account `{floor, ceiling_source: "brief", aimd: {increase: 1, quiet_window_s: 120, decrease: 0.75}, health: {fivexx_threshold: 3, fivexx_window_s: 120, probe_backoff_s: 30, probe_backoff_max_s: 600, probes_to_recover: 2}}`, plus `failure_patterns` (the provider strings) and `priority_classes` (reserved for the deferred admission ordering). |
| **Runtime state** | `watchdog/capacity/state.json` (the record), `watchdog/capacity/health-<account>.json`, `watchdog/capacity/limit-estimate.json`; the three `max-codex*` files are derived outputs of the same writer. |
| **Increase** | `refusals_5m == 0 and deaths_5m == 0 and live >= cap - 1` for a full `quiet_window_s` → `cap += 1`. One slot per window, never more. |
| **Decrease** | On the **first** refusal: `cap = max(floor, min(cap, live_at_first_refusal - 1))`. On a further refusal inside the same window: `cap = max(floor, ceil(cap * 0.75))`. |
| **Endpoint down** | `endpoint_5xx` deaths ≥ 3 within 120 s → health `down`, cap 0 immediately, independent of AIMD. This is the 05:30Z–05:58Z relay-us7 outage that cost 69 sessions and was answered by a human typing `echo 0`. |
| **Recovery** | Half-open: after `probe_backoff_s` (doubling to 10 min) one `codex exec --sandbox read-only`, trivial prompt, that account's `CODEX_HOME`, `timeout 60`, single-flight under a lock. Two consecutive successes → cap 1, then AIMD climbs. One failure doubles the backoff. |
| **Failure behaviour** | `unknown` failure class is **neutral** — neither increase nor decrease — so a provider wording change degrades to today's static behaviour instead of collapsing the cap. A malformed `capacity-policy.json` or `run-mode.json` makes the controller exit nonzero and leave the cap files untouched; the supervisor logs and retries. Two writers are impossible by protocol: the controller is the sole writer, and `watchdog/capacity/hold` (an operator touch-file) freezes the cap where it is without stopping health handling. |
| **Owner input still needed** | Only the brief's `nominal_limit`, `external_reserved`, `endpoint` per key — once, before the run. |

**Undeclared sharers** (the forked Claude session on the owner's Mac) need no
identification: they appear as refusals and AIMD walks the cap down. The gap is recorded
as `external_inferred = nominal_limit - external_reserved - measured_limit` in
`limit-estimate.json` and printed by `status-snapshot.sh`, so a persistent invisible
consumer is a number rather than a mystery.

**Carrying the measurement forward.** `limit-estimate.json` records `measured_limit` (the
highest concurrency sustained ≥10 min with zero refusals) and `observed_refusal_floor`.
`run_mode.py apply` seeds the next run's starting cap at
`min(nominal - external_reserved, last_measured_limit)`, so a run starts *below* the cliff
instead of above it. The measured limits are written into the pause handoff (§5).

### Item 2 — Occupancy: idle slots, dead fixers, a hand-fed queue

Four distinct causes, four mechanisms:

| Cause (observed) | Mechanism | Knob / failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `model_policy.py` rejects an explicit astra request for routine jobs, so the owner's "all workers astra" could only be done by a shim rewrite that made `sessions.jsonl` record `sol` for astra sessions | `models.override` in the brief → `watchdog/model-override` runtime knob + an `override` object accepted by `load_policy`. When active, `select_model` returns `policy.hard_model` for every role/job class and stops rejecting an explicit astra request; `override_mode` and `override_source` travel into the per-session model-policy file and into `sessions.jsonl`. The `sol->astra` rewrite is deleted from the shim. | The override may only narrow **toward** the hard model and may never lower effort. Override-period rows are excluded from the Sol:Astra ratio audit by their `override_mode` field rather than read as violations. |
| `autofix.sh` defaults `MIPSTARRE_FIX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra`, which the policy preflight rejects, so every fixer died at exit 4 before reaching a model | `FIX_MODEL="${MIPSTARRE_FIX_MODEL:-}"` (empty = dispatcher default, which is what the script's own header documents). Genuinely hard fixes use `--job-class escalated --hardness-reason "…"`, not a bare model. | A startup self-check runs `model_policy.py --role prover --job-class general --model "$FIX_MODEL" --field model` once and dies with the policy's own message before any worktree work — one loud line instead of N silent deaths. Same guard in `review.sh`. |
| Lanes serialize behind one global launch lock held across a six-hour wait (~2.4 launches/minute max, and a lane whose cap never opens blocks every other lane) | `lane.sh` polls for a free slot **without** the lock; the lock is taken only around the `dispatch.sh` call; the post-launch `sleep 25` becomes a short jittered hold. One `cap()` definition, reading the per-account caps through `account_router.py`, not a hard-coded 9. The dead `MAXR` is deleted. | A bounded wait; on expiry the lane writes `<N>.needs-attention` with reason `no-slot`, which the janitor and the hourly report see — instead of a silent six-hour sleep. |
| An empty dispatch queue while the main session wrote 25-minute reports | Turn cap from run-mode (8 minutes in `fast`), a file-based `watchdog/main-inbox/` queue the keeper drains on its tick so a nudge never waits for a turn to end, and the standing-report shape of §6 that makes the reports short by construction. | The keeper's goal text is rendered from `run_mode.py show`; it can no longer contain stale literal caps like "primary 0, second 22, total 22". |

Plus **one-writer enforcement**: `dispatch.sh` takes a branch claim
(`$CACHE_ROOT/locks/branch-<branch>.claim`, holding role/pid/session) for the whole
session, refusing with exit 5 and naming the holder unless `--allow-concurrent` is given.
Read-only reviewers are exempt (they do not write the tree, and a lane's own review step
must not refuse against its own prover claim). This is the "two loops on one branch"
(autofix + prover on PR 342) that forced a `git stash push` preamble into every meta wave.

### Item 3 — Progress visibility

See §6. `estimate_post.py` is the single writer of the estimate issue and renders exactly
two lines; prose progress is the main session's standing duty on the progress log, written
into `local/personas/main.md` so it is not dictated in a pause message.

### Item 4 — Merge throughput

See §3.

### Item 5 — Lane-runner defects fixed only in `/tmp`

| Defect | Mechanism | Failure behaviour |

Throughput drops until the janitor runs, which is why the janitor lands before or with this change. |
| Modules outside the `MIPStarRE.QPBT` import closure get no olean, so the per-file pre-push gate failed on every lane | `scripts/check_umbrella_imports.py` as a reachability check inside the existing `local-ci/build` step (§3.6), plus the v20 explicit changed-module build kept as belt-and-braces in `lane.sh` | The check never edits `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean` (the operator serializes re-exports); it lists each unreachable module with the exact `import` line and the re-export file it belongs in. The janitor reports that class for operator repair rather than guessing which worktree to move. |

### Item 6 — Speed tier and schedule

`run.speed` in the brief; `run_mode.py set speed` mid-run; the shim regenerated from the
committed `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-bin-codex` template rather than patched by
an `assert old in s` string surgery against a 90-character substring. The main session's
TUI launcher becomes `local/bin/main-session.sh`, which reads `run_mode.py get` for model,
effort, `CODEX_HOME` and `speed` and invokes `codex` **through the shim path** — the
2026-09-12 launcher `exec`'d an absolute `~/.local/bin/codex` and therefore never received
the speed tier. `launch_qpbt_main.sh` and `main-session-astra-v3.sh` are retired with an
`EVOLUTION.md` entry. Cadence lives in the mode file and the crontab is **regenerated**
from it by `install-crons.sh` (backup, then install from a file under `$W`), never edited
in place by `sed` — the 2026-09-12 pause chain wiped the crontab once through a `sed`
delimiter bug.

### Item 7 — Message delivery to the main session

One tracked `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-say.sh --mode idle|interrupt|terminal`:

- `idle` — the v4 rule that ended the 20-minute hang: idleness judged on the **last four
  non-empty lines only** (a stale "esc to interrupt" in the scrollback must not count).
- `interrupt` — Escape after the grace, send, then `/goal resume`.
- `terminal` — Escape, send, **do not resume**, and write `watchdog/goal-hold` so the
  keeper cannot re-resume. On 2026-09-12 the terminal stop order was sent at 08:19Z and
  the same script auto-resumed the goal at 08:24Z.

`goal-keeper.sh` takes `TURN_MAX` from run-mode, renders its goal text from
`run_mode.py show`, and drains `watchdog/main-inbox/` on its two-minute tick.

**Telemetry honesty.** With the model override in the policy layer (Item 2),
`sessions.jsonl` records the model that actually ran; the shim no longer rewrites it.

### Item 8 — Superseded and duplicate work

`local/bin/pr_janitor.py` (§4) closes a PR only when **both** mechanical conditions hold —
empty three-dot diff against `github/main` **and** the head reachable from main — with one
idempotent `<!-- pr-janitor:superseded -->` comment naming the SHAs. It never closes an
issue and never touches a PR with a nonempty diff. The same pass drops lane state for
branches with no open PR (the 20 stale 1xxx lanes) and refuses a second lane or fix loop
on a branch that already has one. Every retirement is one line in the hourly report.

## 3. Merge-throughput design

Nine merges in 3 h 05 m, gaps of 16–70 minutes. The structural ceiling is
*refresh-then-merge-one*: gate 2b requires `github/main` to be an ancestor of the head
(modulo passive telemetry advances), so each merge invalidates every other refreshed head
and N approved PRs cost N full builds and N CI runs, serialized.

This design **does not touch gate 2b**. The batching fix (a merge train with a locally
re-verified receipt) is a merge-gate change that already has an issue and a PR
(#502 / PR 507) and is deferred to them (§9). Everything below raises throughput without
going near `pr_merge.py`.

### 3.1 Remove the conflict class (the biggest single win)

Append-only telemetry logs conflicted on nearly every merge of main. Two changes:

- **`.gitattributes` at the repository root**, committed, with
  `results/telemetry/*.md merge=union`, `results/telemetry/**/*.md merge=union`,
  `results/telemetry/*.jsonl merge=union`, `results/telemetry/**/*.jsonl merge=union`, and
  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md merge=union`. The operator's 2026-09-12 fix lived in
  `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/info/attributes` on one host and is lost on any fresh
  clone. `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` asserts it is in effect
  (`git check-attr merge -- results/telemetry/events.md`) exactly as it already asserts the
  hooks.
- **Shard the event log.** `telemetry.py event` writes to
  `results/telemetry/events.d/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<session>.md`; two sessions never touch one
  path. `events.md` keeps its full history unchanged (7929 lines are not rewritten) and
  gains a short header pointing at `events.d/`; `telemetry.py events --since` reads both so
  existing readers (`proof-status`, the owner tools) keep working. The new paths are inside
  the `results/telemetry` allowlist `pr_merge._is_tolerated_telemetry_path` already
  tolerates, so sharding does not perturb gate 2b.

### 3.2 Self-repairing refreshes

A failed refresh currently does nothing but `touch pr<N>.failed`; repair existed only as a
`/tmp` one-shot the operator invoked, with a `-mmin -15` window, so anything that failed
more than 15 minutes before a tick was invisible forever and the 2 h marker backoff then
hid the PR from the scan as well.

`merge-daemon.sh` classifies each failed refresh from the lane log —
`merging github/main conflicted` → `merge`, `lake build … failed` → `build`,
`pre-push gate failed` → `preflight`, `Reconnecting... 5/5` / 503 / concurrency → `infra` —
and hands `merge` and `build` to the janitor's repair path (§4), one attempt per
`(PR, head)`. Infra failures are retried, not repaired. Repair concurrency shares the PAR
budget so repairs cannot starve merges.

### 3.3 Markers that carry a reason

`pr<N>.failed` becomes a JSON record `{pr, head, ts, class, reason, attempts, lane_log}`.
Backoff by class: `infra` 5 min; `conflict`/`build` until the repair finishes;
`preflight` 15 min; `gate` until the head changes. Automatic clearing keys on an
observable change, never on elapsed time alone:

- the PR head SHA changed, or
- the recorded reason string no longer appears in a dry run of the failing step, or
- the installed `tools-version` (§7) is newer than the marker, which clears every
  `preflight`/`build` marker — this is exactly the 05:44Z situation where eleven unrelated
  PRs stayed blocked after the systemic lane bugs had been fixed, and was answered by
  `rm` and by `( sleep 1500; rm -f … )`.

Every live marker with its reason is one line in the hourly report (§6), so a stuck marker
is never silent.

### 3.4 Parallelism sized by the machine, and one build at a time

`PAR` was a hand-typed constant (default 1; set to 8 at 05:44Z) on a host at load 90–150
shared with other users, while each refresh lane started a **full `lake build` outside**
`ci.sh`'s machine-wide lock and then queued on that lock in CI. Two changes:

- `PAR = clamp(1, floor((nproc - load1) / cores_per_build), free_worker_slots)`,
  re-evaluated every loop, `cores_per_build` a single knob in
  `results/telemetry/owner-tools/daemon.conf` (default 16). The chosen PAR and its inputs
  are logged on every scan line.
- The lane's pre-push build goes through the same lock helper `ci.sh` uses, restoring
  DESIGN.md invariant 7 ("at most one full `lake build` machine-wide"). A single lane is
  slower in the worst case; N lanes stop thrashing the NVMe cache and the CI queue.

### 3.5 Retire what should not be a candidate

The retirement pass of §2 Item 8 runs inside the daemon scan: a PR already on main never
enters a candidate list again, never absorbs a refresh or a review re-run, and never
inflates the ready-but-open count the owner is asked to interpret.

### 3.6 Reachability guard

`scripts/check_umbrella_imports.py` walks `MIPStarRE/**/*.lean` (excluding `*/Test/*`),
computes the transitive import closure of the re-export roots (`MIPStarRE.lean`,
`MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`, `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean` and the per-directory re-export files AGENTS.md
requires to be preserved), and exits nonzero listing each unreachable module with the
exact `import` line and the re-export file it belongs in. It runs inside the **existing**
`local-ci/build` step, so the eight canonical contexts and therefore `pr_merge.py` gate 3
are unchanged. A PR that introduces an orphan fails in CI, not three hours later in a lane.

### 3.7 Measure it

`results/telemetry/merge-latency.jsonl`, one row per state transition
(`{pr, head, event: ready|refresh_start|refresh_end|merged|failed, class, reason, seconds, par}`),
written by the daemon and by `ready_report.py`. The hourly report prints merges/hour,
median ready-to-merged minutes and the top blocking class — the "is it progressing?"

## 4. The self-repair janitor

`local/bin/janitor.sh` — one idempotent pass, safe to run from cron or from the daemon
loop, keyed on record fields and never on date globs (the 2026-09-12 recovery script
globbed `*20260912*.jsonl` and filtered lane numbers with `/[0-9]{3}\.needs-attention$`,
so lanes below 100 and the 1xxx lanes were never repaired).

| Pass | Input | Action | Cap / ledger |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dead sessions** | `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` rows with `status: active` whose pid is dead (`account_router.live_pids`) and whose capture ends in an exhausted reconnect / 5xx / concurrency refusal | re-dispatch the same role on the same PR **and the same head**; mark the abandoned row `failed` so telemetry stops showing it live | at most 2 per `(pr, role, head_sha)`, ledger `watchdog/janitor/retries.jsonl`. Never re-dispatch a session whose capture shows a clean end. |
| **Parked lanes** | `watchdog/lanes/*.needs-attention`, no digit or age filter | classify the recorded reason (`merge conflicted` / `build failed` / `gate failed` / `no commits ahead` / `uncommitted worker changes` / `worktree-mismatch` / `no-slot`); dispatch an orc for the first two with the brief from `local/briefs/lane-repair-merge.md` / `lane-repair-build.md`; relaunch the tail via `local/bin/lane.sh` with `SKIP_DISPATCH=1` | 2 repairs per lane; the worktree must be clean and not mid-merge before a relaunch; classes it cannot fix stay parked and appear in the report |
| **Superseded PRs** | every open PR | `pr_janitor.py`: close only when the three-dot diff against `github/main` is empty **and** the head is reachable from main, with one idempotent marker comment | never closes an issue; anything else goes to the report |
| **Stale lane state** | `watchdog/lanes/<N>.*` | delete for lanes whose PR is closed or merged | — |
| **Spool expiry** | `watchdog/capacity/spool/*.json` | drop entries past the run's `dispatch_cutoff` | — |

The repair briefs are committed text, not shell string literals, and keep the current
constraints verbatim: *never drop a theorem or a proof; no sorry, no admit, no new axiom;
check every touched file with `lake env lean`; do not push (the lane pushes)*. A repair
that deletes paths main carries still fails the lane's post-merge `merge_loss_guard` check
— that guard is untouched.

**Retry and spool on the dispatch side.** `dispatch.sh` writes the full request (role,
issue, worktree, persona ref, effort, job class, prompt path, attempt, deadline) to
`watchdog/capacity/spool/<name>.json` **before** reserving. On a `refused` /
`concurrency_limit` / `endpoint_5xx` / `retries_exhausted` outcome it does not exit: it
sleeps a jittered exponential backoff (base 30 s, cap 10 min) and re-reserves, up to
`MIPSTARRE_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS` (default 5) or the dispatch cutoff, then exits with a
distinct code leaving the spool entry for the janitor. Router refusal becomes retryable
rather than `die 4`.

Two safety rules on that retry, both load-bearing:

1. **A transient-class retry never consumes a proof packet attempt** and never resets its
   budget; the budget fields in `account_router.continuation()` are untouched and the
   retried dispatch reuses the same name with an attempt suffix so telemetry keeps one
   episode.
2. **A retry is gated on endpoint health.** A retry against an account whose
   `health-<account>.json` says `down` waits for half-open; it does not fire. Five
   client-side retries are precisely how 69 refusals became 69 deaths.

## 5. Pause within 15 minutes, and resume

One tracked script, `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-pause.sh [--deadline 15m] [--reason …]`,
replacing the four `/tmp` variants (`owner-pause.sh`, `owner-pause-v2.sh`,
`owner-pause-fast.sh`, `final-pause.sh`) whose chain hard-coded a timestamp, edited the
crontab three times in sequence without a backup, and clobbered the saved caps.

**Phases** (offsets from the owner's word; the deadline comes from
`run.pause_deadline_min`, default 15):

| T | Phase | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| +0:00 | Stop admission | `run_mode.py pause` → caps to 0 **and the pre-pause caps saved inside `capacity/state.json`** (not in a second file that a later phase can clobber); `touch watchdog/drain`. |
| +0:30 | Release waiters | `account_router.reserve` checks `watchdog/drain` each loop and exits cleanly with a distinct status, so queued dispatches release themselves instead of being `kill`ed (49 waiters were observed at 06:38Z). Stop keeper, merge daemon (stop file kept) and stack-watch by their stop files and pids. |
| +1:00 | One terminal message | `owner-say.sh --mode terminal`: "post the closing progress comment and write the handoff; do not post prose on the estimate issue; then `/goal pause`". No auto-resume, `watchdog/goal-hold` written. The *content* of the closing report is not dictated here — it is a standing duty in `local/personas/main.md` (§6). |
| +2:00 | Crontab | Back up `crontab -l` verbatim to `$W/crontab.<ts>.bak`, **failing the phase if `crontab -l` returns nothing**, then install the paused crontab from a file under `$W`. Never in-place `sed`, never from `/tmp`. |
| deadline −2:00 | Kill leftovers | Anchored patterns only (`^bash <owner-bin>/lane.sh `, `^bash [^ ]*autofix\.sh`, fix-lane, conflict-resolve, dispatchers, `python3 [^ ]*account_router\.py`, `^node [^ ]*codex(\.js)?( \|$).* exec( \|$)`): SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 20 s. Partial work stays in the worker's worktree; never `git clean`. |
| deadline | Confirm and record | Confirm `Goal paused` in the pane; write `watchdog/pause-state.json`; append `stages.jsonl` + an `events.d/` entry; commit and push telemetry. |

`pause-state.json` is the single record:
`{caps: {…, taken from run-mode, not from the already-zeroed live files}, speed,
estimate_cadence_min, crontab_backup, crontab_sha256, daemon_par, run_mode: {…},
measured_limits: {…}, main_goal: "paused", paused_at}`.

**Resume** — `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-resume.sh`, run only on the owner's word,
restores **from that record only**:

1. `run_mode.py resume` restores caps and speed and re-enters AIMD at the saved value.
2. `crontab "$W/crontab.<ts>.bak"` verbatim — no `sed` un-commenting. The 2026-09-12
   resume script's `sed -E 's#^\#PAUSED-2026[0-9]{4} ##'` would have resurrected the
   watchdog / astra-poll / heartbeat crons that have been deliberately commented since
   2026-09-09. If the live crontab differs from the sha the pause recorded, the script
   **refuses and prints the difference** rather than overwriting the owner's edits.
3. Restart daemon, stack-watch, keeper; deliver one resume message rendered from
   `run_mode.py show` (the current script hard-codes "primary 5 / second 39 / total 44",
   already wrong by 04:58Z on the day it ran).
4. Post-condition check: every cap file exists, is numeric and nonzero for an enabled
   account, health is not `down`, `watchdog/drain` is gone. A failure here is loud.

| Channel | Content | Writer | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Estimate issue (`run.estimate_issue`, #168) | **Exactly two lines**: the bold headline `**<ts> — implemented ≈ N% · days to go ≈ D**` and one `<sub>` provenance line. Nothing else, ever. | `local/bin/estimate_post.py`, called by `estimate.sh` from cron | `estimate_post.py` renders the body itself and refuses any other body. The issue number comes from run-mode and is validated at briefing time, so a missing `watchdog/estimate-issue` can no longer silently no-op the owner's only progress channel. `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` §6 and `local/personas/main.md` state the rule, so it survives the session that heard it. |
| Progress log (`run.progress_issue`, #27) | (a) One five-line progress comment every 30 minutes in `fast` mode: merges since the last post, live workers vs the occupancy floor, holes on main, the next three critical packets, blockers. (b) One hourly readiness report. (c) One line per stage boundary, merge, adopted mathematical correction, automatic PR retirement and repair. | (a) and (c) the main session as a standing duty in `local/personas/main.md`; (b) `local/bin/ready_report.py` from cron | The 30-minute comment is **skipped, not padded**, when nothing changed since the previous post. |
| Owner inbox (`run.owner_inbox_issue`, #500) | Permission, credential, access or scope grants only; ten plain lines; one id. Never progress, never a project-outcome decision. | main session | Unchanged rule; this design only sweeps the stale `#26` references out of `main.md`, `issues-prs.md`, `orchestrator.md`, `mathfix.md`, `sessions.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `status-snapshot.sh` label (which prints "#26 open blockers" while querying issue 500). |

**The readiness report** (`ready_report.py`) is the mechanism for the owner's rule *"a
ready-to-merge PR left open needs a good reason"*. For every open PR it computes readiness
from the exact head (`local-ci/summary`, `local-review/summary`, unchecked ledger lines,
`CHANGES_REQUESTED`, draft) and, for each ready-but-open PR, **the reason it has not
merged, read from daemon state rather than guessed**: stale (base moved, minutes since),
refreshing (pid, lane, elapsed), failed marker (class + reason string), awaiting
adjudication, or `unexplained`. `unexplained` is the alarm case and should always be zero.
Output: one comment per hour on the progress issue in the form
`ready N, merged-this-hour M` plus one line per ready-but-open PR, and the same rows
appended to `merge-latency.jsonl`. A post is suppressed when the ready set and the reasons
are byte-identical to the previous hour and nothing merged, and forced at least every
6 hours.

**The closing report** is a standing duty, not a pause-message dictation: one comment on
the progress issue plus `results/telemetry/owner-handoffs/<date>-main.md` from the
committed `TEMPLATE.md`, **with every number measured by the session itself**
(`status-snapshot.sh`, `gh`) rather than copied from the operator's message — the
2026-09-12 handoff reads "Owner listed eight merges" because the operator's message was
the source.

## 7. What stays outside the repository, and how it is installed

Some things cannot live in the repository: they drive tmux, the crontab and the host's
process table, and they must be usable while the repository is mid-merge. On 2026-09-12
they lived in `/tmp` under names that no longer described their contents (`lane-v17.sh`
was really v20; `merge-daemon-v9h.sh` called `/tmp/merge-v2.sh`, a file that does not even
exist in the snapshot), were patched in place by `assert anchor in src` Python here-docs,
and ran in three simultaneous versions.

**The rule.** Operator scripts live in the repository under
`results/telemetry/owner-tools/` at honest names with a version header, and are **deployed**
to the host by one versioned installer. They are never edited on the host.

`results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh`:

```
install.sh [--force] [--compat-tmp] [--crons] [--dry-run]
```

1. Copies each tool from the checkout to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/`.
2. Writes a manifest `owner-bin/tools-version` (git describe + SHA, timestamp) and
   `owner-bin/manifest.sha256` with the SHA-256 of every installed file.
3. **Refuses** to overwrite a deployed copy whose hash matches no released version — a
   hand patch is detected, not silently clobbered. `--force` overwrites and moves the
   previous copy to `owner-bin/attic/<ts>/` rather than deleting it.
4. `--compat-tmp` additionally creates `/tmp/<name>.sh` **symlinks** into `owner-bin/`, so
   anything still invoking a historical `/tmp` path runs versioned code and nothing is ever
   edited in `/tmp`.
5. `--crons` calls `install-crons.sh`, which regenerates the whole crontab from run-mode
   (estimate every 30 min when `speed=fast`, every 6 h otherwise; readiness report hourly;
   the nudging crons left exactly as the mode file says), always backup-then-install from a
   file under `$W`. It never `sed`s the live crontab and it fails if `crontab -l` returns
   nothing.
6. Every tool prints `tool=<name> version=<sha>` as its first log line and records it in
   the lane's `.done` / `.needs-attention` marker, so a lane log names the code that
   produced it.
7. The daemon **refuses to start** (and posts one progress-log line) when a dependency is
   missing or its hash does not match the manifest, instead of failing per PR at merge
   time.

Inventory of what is installed rather than run from the checkout:

| Installed tool | Source of truth | Why outside `local/bin` |
|---|---|---|
| `merge-daemon.sh`, `merge.sh`, `daemon-scan.py`, `daemon.conf` | `results/telemetry/owner-tools/` | long-running host loop, must survive a mid-merge checkout |
| `owner-pause.sh`, `owner-resume.sh`, `owner-say.sh`, `goal-keeper.sh`, `install-crons.sh` | idem | drive tmux and the crontab |
| `capacityd.sh`, `status-snapshot.sh`, `estimate.sh` | idem | host loops / host census |
| `owner-bin-codex` (the PATH shim template) | idem | a PATH shim by construction |
| `local/bin/*` (dispatch, lane, janitor, ci, review, autofix, run_mode, capacity_controller, ready_report, estimate_post, pr_janitor) | the checkout, invoked by its **primary-checkout path** | pipeline scripts; a worktree copy can predate protocol fixes |

The owner's personal cron scripts that remain in `~/bin` get an entry in
`results/telemetry/owner-tools/README.md` naming their installed path and source of truth.

1. **Merge train (`local/bin/pr_train.py`, gate 2b batching; audits MT1 and MT8).** This is
   the largest single throughput win and it is *not* rejected — it is out of scope here
   because it adds a new pass condition to `pr_merge.py` gate 2b, the staleness gate, and
   because it already has issue #502 and PR 507 (design-decisions D1, 2026-09-09 09:05).
   A second PR for the same issue would violate one-PR-per-issue. Constraints this design
   records for that PR: the receipt must be re-verified by recomputing the merge locally
   and never trusted as a file; it must name exact SHAs and be refused if the base moved;
   gates 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 stay per-PR and unchanged; the train must assert the post-train
   `github/main^{tree}` equals the integration tree and stop with a report if it does not;
   candidates ordered by fewest changed files with conflicting heads dropped to the repair
   path; `train_max` default 8 with a bisect fallback so one bad PR does not drop the
   innocent ones.
2. **Priority-ordered admission and `drain --to N` (audit CAP-11).** Ordering waiters by
   role class and cancelling low-priority waiters back into the spool is valuable — 49
   waiters were observed behind 12 workers — but `account_router.reserve` is on the hot path
   of every dispatch and a regression there stops all work. Land it as a follow-up issue
   after W3 is running, with age escalation against starvation and tests for the existing
   invariants (dead-marker reaping, dry-run reserves nothing, explicit accounts never spill).
3. **The estimate-issue reformat guard (audit OI-5 second half).** Editing another
   session's GitHub comment is destructive and needs an explicit owner decision. The
   single-writer half (`estimate_post.py` refusing any non-conforming body) is in W1; the
   `--guard` that rewrites an offending comment is not.
4. **Any change to `.githooks/*`, `merge_loss_guard.py`, `checked-push.sh`, the seven
   `pr_merge.py` gates, the eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts, or the review-verdict
   contract.** Out of scope by rule. Note that W5 *removes* a bypass of the pre-push hook
   rather than changing it, which is permitted and is the point.
5. **Retiring `max-codex` entirely.** It is inert for admission but live for the lane
   runner's internal parallelism and for the operator display. W3 makes it a derived value
   with a documented "no admission meaning"; deleting it is a separate cleanup.
6. **Changing the Sol:Astra ratio policy, the `cores_per_build` default, the occupancy
   target, the estimate denominator (197), or the review round caps.** All owner or
   main-session policy decisions, not workflow mechanisms. `cores_per_build` ships as a
   config default of 16 so no one is asked a question at run time.
7. **A supervisor/service manager for the host loops.** `capacityd.sh` is a 20-line
   `while true; do …; sleep 60; done` started by the installer. Anything more is the
   "hardening the hardening" pattern that cost this project 17 hours on 2026-09-01.

   360	        where = f"accounts[{index}]"
   361	        _require_mapping(raw, where)
   362	        unknown = sorted(set(raw) - set(ACCOUNT_KEYS))
   363	        if unknown:
   364	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.{unknown[0]}",
   365	                             f"unknown key(s) under {where}: {', '.join(unknown)}")
   366	        missing = [key for key in ACCOUNT_KEYS if key not in raw]
   367	        if missing:
   368	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.{missing[0]}",
   369	                             f"{where} is missing: {', '.join(missing)}")
   370	        name = _require_text(raw["name"], f"{where}.name")
   371	        if name not in ACCOUNT_NAMES:
   372	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.name",
   373	                             f"account name {name!r} is outside {ACCOUNT_NAMES}; "
   374	                             "account_router.py knows exactly these two")
   375	        if name in seen:
   376	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.name", f"account {name!r} is listed twice")
   377	        seen.add(name)
   378	        endpoint = _require_text(raw["endpoint"], f"{where}.endpoint", pattern=ENDPOINT_RE)
   379	        codex_home = _require_text(raw["codex_home"], f"{where}.codex_home")
   380	        nominal = _require_int(raw["nominal_limit"], f"{where}.nominal_limit", minimum=1)
   381	        reserved = _require_int(raw["external_reserved"], f"{where}.external_reserved", minimum=0)
   382	        if reserved >= nominal:
   383	            raise BriefError(
   384	                f"{where}.external_reserved",
   385	                f"{where}: external_reserved {reserved} leaves no slot below "
   386	                f"nominal_limit {nominal}; nominal_limit is a ceiling for the whole key, "
   387	                "and the pipeline's share is nominal_limit - external_reserved")

   389	        if not isinstance(enabled, bool):
   390	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.enabled",
   391	                             f"{where}.enabled must be true or false, got {enabled!r}")
   392	        out.append({
   393	            "name": name,
   394	            "label": _require_text(raw["label"], f"{where}.label", pattern=ENDPOINT_RE),
   395	            "endpoint": endpoint,
   396	            "codex_home": codex_home,
   397	            "codex_home_path": str(Path(codex_home).expanduser()),
   398	            "nominal_limit": nominal,
   399	            "external_reserved": reserved,
   400	            "enabled": enabled,
   401	        })
   402	    if not any(account["enabled"] for account in out):
   403	        raise BriefError("accounts", "no account is enabled; the run would dispatch nowhere")

   421	def resolve_override(speed: str, briefed: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
   422	    """The override actually in force for *speed*, and where it came from.
   423	
   424	    A briefed ``null`` resolves from the speed tier: ``fast`` is ``astra-all``,
   425	    because in full speed mode every role — reviewers included — runs the hard
   426	    model.  ``"policy"`` is how a fast run says "leave the published policy
   427	    alone"; it is deliberately a word rather than the absence of one, so the
   428	    file records a decision instead of an omission.
   429	    """
   430	    published = "published local/model-policy.json"
   431	    if briefed == "policy":
   432	        return (None, f"brief: models.override 'policy' ({published})")
   433	    if briefed is not None:
   434	        return (briefed, "brief: models.override")
   435	    resolved = SPEED_DEFAULT_OVERRIDE.get(speed)
   436	    if resolved is None:
   437	        return (None, f"default for run.speed {speed} ({published})")
   438	    return (resolved, f"default for run.speed {speed} (every role, reviewers included)")

   496	def measured_limits(root: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
   497	    """Per-account `measured_limit` from the capacity controller, if any.
   498	
   499	    An unreadable or malformed estimate degrades to "no measurement" with a
   500	    warning: a corrupt runtime file must never become zero capacity.
   501	    """
   502	    base = root or cache_root()
   503	    path = base / "watchdog" / "capacity" / "limit-estimate.json"
   504	    if not path.exists():
   505	        return {}
   506	    try:
   507	        doc = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   508	    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   509	        sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: warning: ignoring {path}: {exc}\n")
   510	        return {}
   511	    accounts = doc.get("accounts") if isinstance(doc, dict) else None
   512	    source = accounts if isinstance(accounts, dict) else doc if isinstance(doc, dict) else {}
   513	    out: dict[str, int] = {}
   514	    for name in ACCOUNT_NAMES:
   515	        row = source.get(name)
   516	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
   517	            continue
   518	        value = row.get("measured_limit")
   519	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
   520	            continue
   521	        out[name] = value
   522	    return out

   525	def effective_caps(brief: dict, measured: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
   526	    """Starting cap per account.
   527	
   528	    ``cap0 = clamp(1, nominal_limit - external_reserved,
   529	    last_measured_limit or nominal_limit - external_reserved)`` — a run starts
   530	    below the measured cliff instead of above it.  A disabled or unlisted
   531	    account is 0: the pipeline never dispatches there at all.
   532	    """
   533	    seen = measured or {}
   534	    caps = {name: 0 for name in ACCOUNT_NAMES}
   535	    for account in brief["accounts"]:
   536	        if not account["enabled"]:
   537	            continue
   538	        base = account["nominal_limit"] - account["external_reserved"]
   539	        target = base
   540	        limit = seen.get(account["name"])
   541	        if isinstance(limit, int) and limit >= 0:
   542	            target = min(base, limit)
   543	        caps[account["name"]] = max(1, min(base, target))
   544	    return caps

   548	    return int(occupancy_target * sum(caps.values()))

   551	def cap_values(caps: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
   552	    """The three derived files; `max-codex` is mechanically the sum.
   553	
   554	    Values are validated, never coerced: a string or ``None`` reaching a cap
   555	    file is the failure this refuses, so it must not be silently repaired.
   556	    """
   557	    values: dict[str, int] = {}
   558	    for name in ACCOUNT_NAMES:
   559	        value = caps.get(name, 0)
   560	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
   561	            raise LayerError(f"refusing max-codex-{name}: {value!r} is not a "
   562	                             "nonnegative integer (an empty or non-numeric cap file "
   563	                             "makes every dispatch exit 4)")
   564	        values[f"max-codex-{name}"] = value
   565	    values["max-codex"] = sum(values.values())
   566	    return values

   590	def write_model_override(mode: dict, *, root: Path | None = None,
   591	                         dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
   592	    """Make the resolved ``models.override`` real: write or remove the knob.
   593	
   594	    Validating the field and exposing it through ``get model_override`` is not
   595	    the same as applying it. Until this ran, ``models.override`` was inert: the
   596	    only live overrides were the committed ``local/model-policy.json`` (a
   597	    reviewed PR, impossible mid-run) and a knob file a human typed — so "every
   598	    worker on the hard model" still cost a hand edit, the intervention the field
   599	    exists to remove.  What is written is the EFFECTIVE override
   600	    (``mode_override``), not the briefed word: a fast run with no override in
   601	    the brief still puts every role on the hard model.
   602	    """
   603	    path = (root or cache_root()) / MODEL_OVERRIDE_REL
   604	    override, source = mode_override(mode)
   605	    if dry_run:
   606	        return (f"{path} removed (no override; {source})" if override is None
   607	                else f"{path} = {override} ({source})")
   608	    if override is None:
   609	        try:
   610	            path.unlink()
   611	        except FileNotFoundError:
   612	            return "no model override (runtime knob absent)"
   613	        except OSError as exc:
   614	            raise LayerError(f"cannot remove the model override knob {path}: {exc}") from exc
   615	        return f"model override cleared ({path} removed)"
   616	    document = {"mode": override,
   617	                "set_by": f"run_mode.py, brief sha256 {mode['brief_sha256'][:12]}",
   618	                "reason": source}
   619	    atomic_write(path, json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
   620	    return f"model override {override} active ({source}; runtime knob {path})"

   628	def account_mode(mode: dict) -> str:
   629	    """`both` when the second account is enabled, `primary` otherwise.
   630	
   631	    DERIVED, never briefed.  The shim's `primary-only policy` check was a second
   632	    file holding a capacity decision: with the file absent it defaults to
   633	    `primary`, and every dispatch whose CODEX_HOME is not ~/.codex exits 4.  So a
   634	    brief that enabled `second` with a nominal_limit of 30 could dispatch nowhere
   635	    on that key while the capacity controller kept a cap of 28 and AIMD saw only
   636	    deaths — the idle-slot failure of 2026-09-12 intervention 2, with no message
   637	    anywhere saying why.  `accounts[].enabled` is the ONE place that decision
   638	    lives (full-speed-mode.md section 1: every number the owner states lives in
   639	    exactly one file), and this function is the only thing that derives the file
   640	    from it.
   641	    """
   642	    second = next((a for a in mode.get("accounts", []) if a.get("name") == "second"), {})
   643	    return "both" if second.get("enabled") else "primary"

   650	    wanted = account_mode(mode)
   651	    names = ", ".join(a["name"] for a in mode.get("accounts", []) if a.get("enabled")) or "none"
   652	    note = f"{path} = {wanted} (enabled accounts: {names})"
   653	    if dry_run:
   654	        return note

   659	                         "the PATH shim refuses every non-default CODEX_HOME while "
   660	                         "this file says 'primary'")

   664	def read_live_caps(root: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, int | None]:
   665	    """Cap files as the router sees them; unreadable is None, never zero."""
   666	    base = (root or cache_root()) / "watchdog"
   667	    out: dict[str, int | None] = {}
   668	    for name in ACCOUNT_NAMES:
   669	        path = base / f"max-codex-{name}"
   670	        try:
   671	            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
   672	        except OSError:
   673	            out[name] = None
   674	            continue
   675	        if not text.isdigit():

   678	                             "not as zero\n")
   679	            out[name] = None

   689	def build_mode(brief: dict, digest: str, source: Path,
   690	               caps: dict[str, int], measured: dict[str, int]) -> dict:
   691	    run = dict(brief["run"])

   696	        row["base_cap"] = account["nominal_limit"] - account["external_reserved"]
   697	        row["measured_limit"] = measured.get(account["name"])

   703	        "brief_sha256": digest,
   704	        "run": run,
   705	        "accounts": accounts,
   706	        "models": resolved_models(brief["models"]["override"], run["speed"]),
   707	        "derived": {
   708	            "caps": dict(caps),
   709	            "max_codex": sum(caps.values()),
   710	            "floor": floor_for(caps, run["occupancy_target"]),
   711	        },
   712	        "paused": False,
   713	        "paused_at": None,

     2	# dispatch.sh — the only sanctioned way to start a codex agent session.
     3	#
     4	# Usage:
     5	#   local/bin/dispatch.sh --role <orc|prover|reviewer|simplifier|blueprint|splitter|scout|mathfix>
     6	#                         --issue <id|scope>
     7	#                         [--worktree DIR]        working root (default: repo root)

     9	#                         [--persona FILE]        repo-relative => read from the trusted ref
    10	#                         [--persona-ref REF]     trusted ref for personas (default: main)
    11	#                         [--no-persona]          dispatch with the built-in role frame only
    12	#                         [--resume THREAD_ID]    continue an existing codex thread
    13	#                         [--continue-from FILE]  fresh primary checkpoint/budget handoff JSON
    14	#                         [--account ACCOUNT]     auto|primary|second (default auto)
    15	#                         [--effort LEVEL]        model_reasoning_effort override
    16	#                         [--job-class CLASS]     bounded audit-backed job class
    17	#                         [--context-file FILE]   untrusted data to attach (repeatable)
    18	#                         [--pr ID]               PR id recorded in the registry line
    19	#                         [--skip-hook-check]     do not install/verify git hooks
    20	#                         [--lock-wait SECONDS]   wait for a busy worktree (default 0)
    21	#                         [--allow-concurrent]    do not take the branch claim
    22	#                         [--dry-run]             print the composed prompt and exit
    23	#                         -- "task prompt"
    24	#
    25	# Replaces the parent repository's GitHub-hosted agent entry points: the
    26	# @claude/@codex mention responder (.github/workflows/claude.yml) and the
    27	# agent invocations inside pr-review.yml / auto-fix.yml, whose bot identity,
    28	# trusted-prompt checkout and run accounting came from GitHub. Locally the
    29	# equivalents are: this script's single entry point (identity), `git show
    30	# <ref>:<path>` for personas (trusted prompts, DESIGN.md invariant 5), and
    31	# results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (accounting, DESIGN.md "Agent sessions").
    32	#
    33	# What it does, in order:
    34	#   1. validates the role, sanitizes the scope (bracket-free naming),
    35	#      resolves the sandbox default, honours LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED;
    36	#   2. allocates a session name <role>-<scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq> under a lock;
    37	#   3. installs/verifies the per-worktree git hooks for write sessions;
    38	#   4. composes the prompt: persona (from the trusted ref) + session context
    39	#      + sanitized untrusted attachments + the task;
    40	#   5. claims the worktree's branch, spools the request, and then, per attempt:
    41	#      refuses a `down` endpoint, reserves an account slot, runs
    42	#      `codex exec --json -C <worktree> --sandbox <mode> </dev/null`, tees live
    43	#      events to the cache and publishes the final capture to
    44	#      results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl;
    45	#   6. appends the registry line via local/bin/telemetry.py and prints name,
    46	#      thread_id, the last-message path, the failure class and the attempt count.
    47	#
    48	# Spool and retry (local/protocols/sessions.md §4.1).  A provider refusal is a
    49	# condition of the day, not a defect of the task: the full request is written to
    50	# $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/capacity/spool/<name>.json BEFORE the first reservation,
    51	# and a `refused` / `concurrency_limit` / `endpoint_5xx` / `retries_exhausted`
    52	# outcome is retried after a jittered exponential backoff (base 30 s, cap 10 min)
    53	# up to MIPSTARRE_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS or the run's dispatch cutoff.  Two rules are
    54	# load-bearing:
    55	#   * a transient-class retry NEVER consumes a proof packet attempt and never
    56	#     resets a budget — the continuation handoff is validated once, before the
    57	#     loop, and the retried dispatch reuses the same name with an `-a<N>` suffix

    62	#     became 69 deaths on 2026-09-12.

    64	# diagnostic evidence until janitor expiry and the exit status is 7. Neither

   124	release_locks() {

   127	    for dir in "${LOCKS_HELD[@]}"; do

   154	acquire_lock() {
   155	  # acquire_lock <name> <wait-seconds> <purpose>
   156	  local name="$1" wait_s="$2" purpose="$3"
   157	  local dir="$LOCK_DIR/$name.lock"
   158	  local waited=0 owner=""
   159	  mkdir -p "$LOCK_DIR"
   160	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   161	    owner="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   162	    if [ -n "$owner" ] && ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
   163	      note "breaking stale lock $dir (pid $owner is gone)"
   164	      rm -rf "$dir"
   165	      continue
   166	    fi
   167	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   168	      die 5 "$purpose is locked by pid ${owner:-unknown} ($dir).
   169	  Another dispatch is writing there. Wait, or pass --lock-wait SECONDS.
   170	  Only one writing session per worktree (DESIGN.md invariant 1, single writer)."
   171	    fi
   172	    sleep 2
   173	    waited=$((waited + 2))
   174	  done
   175	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   176	  date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z >"$dir/since"
   177	  LOCKS_HELD[${#LOCKS_HELD[@]}]="$dir"
   178	}

   180	release_one_lock() {
   181	  # Release exactly one held lock. The session-name allocator is released as
   182	  # soon as the number is minted, while the worktree lock and the branch claim
   183	  # must survive every retry of the same session.
   184	  local dir="$1" held
   185	  local kept=()
   186	  rm -f "$dir/pid" "$dir/since" "$dir/role" "$dir/session" 2>/dev/null || true
   187	  rmdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true
   188	  if [ "${#LOCKS_HELD[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   189	    for held in "${LOCKS_HELD[@]}"; do
   190	      [ "$held" = "$dir" ] || kept[${#kept[@]}]="$held"
   191	    done
   192	  fi
   193	  LOCKS_HELD=("${kept[@]+"${kept[@]}"}")
   194	}

   196	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   197	# Branch claim — one writer per BRANCH, not merely per worktree
   198	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   199	# A branch can be checked out in more than one worktree, and on 2026-09-12 an
   200	# autofix loop and a prover ran on PR 342's branch at once; every meta wave then
   201	# needed a `git stash push` preamble. The worktree lock cannot see that, so the
   202	# claim is keyed on the branch and names its holder when it refuses.
   203	# Read-only sessions are exempt: they write nothing, and a lane's own review
   204	# step must not refuse against its own prover's claim.
   205	
   206	safe_component() {
   207	  printf '%s' "$1" | tr '/' '-' | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '-'
   208	}
   209	
   210	claim_branch() {
   211	  # claim_branch <branch>
   212	  local branch="$1"
   213	  local dir owner="" holder_role="" holder_session=""
   214	  dir="$LOCK_DIR/branch-$(safe_component "$branch").claim"
   215	  mkdir -p "$LOCK_DIR"
   216	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   217	    owner="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   218	    if [ -n "$owner" ] && ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
   219	      note "breaking stale branch claim $dir (pid $owner is gone)"
   220	      rm -rf "$dir"
   221	      continue
   222	    fi
   223	    holder_role="$(cat "$dir/role" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   224	    holder_session="$(cat "$dir/session" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   225	    die 5 "branch '$branch' is claimed by session ${holder_session:-unknown} \
   226	(role ${holder_role:-unknown}, pid ${owner:-unknown}).
   227	  Two writers on one branch produce interleaved commits and a stash-and-hope
   228	  recovery (events.md 2026-09-12, PR 342). Wait for that session, or pass
   229	  --allow-concurrent if you have a reason and can name it."
   230	  done
   231	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   232	  printf '%s\n' "$ROLE" >"$dir/role"
   233	  printf '%s\n' "$NAME" >"$dir/session"
   234	  date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z >"$dir/since"
   235	  LOCKS_HELD[${#LOCKS_HELD[@]}]="$dir"
   236	  BRANCH_CLAIM="$dir"
   237	}

   967	write_spool() {

   969	  # diagnostic evidence until janitor expiry. Replay is bounded to this running
   970	  # dispatch; the spool is not a command for automatic post-exit delivery.

   978	    "$CONTINUATION_FILE" "$KEY_LABEL" "$ENDPOINT_LABEL" "$FAILURE_CLASS" <<'PY'
   979	import json, os, sys, tempfile, time
   980	
   981	KEYS = ("state", "base_name", "name", "role", "issue", "pr", "worktree", "branch",
   982	        "persona", "persona_ref", "effort", "job_class", "hardness_reason",
   983	        "prompt_file", "sandbox", "account", "attempt", "max_attempts",
   984	        "deadline_epoch", "dispatcher", "resume", "continue_from", "key_label",
   985	        "endpoint", "failure_class")

   991	record["attempt"] = int(record["attempt"] or 1)
   992	record["max_attempts"] = int(record["max_attempts"] or 1)
   993	record["deadline_epoch"] = int(record["deadline_epoch"]) if record["deadline_epoch"] else None
   994	record["spooled_at"] = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z")

   998	                                     dir=os.path.dirname(path), delete=False)
   999	try:
  1000	    json.dump(record, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
  1001	    handle.write("\n")
  1002	    handle.flush()

  1005	    handle.close()

  1022	retry_is_safe() {
  1023	  # A transient CLASS is not by itself a licence to re-run the prompt.
  1024	  # `refused`, `endpoint_down`, `concurrency_limit` and `endpoint_5xx` are
  1025	  # admission failures: the model never ran, the worktree was never touched, and
  1026	  # a retry is a pure re-attempt.  `retries_exhausted` is different — the client
  1027	  # gave up reconnecting, which can happen twenty minutes in, and re-running the
  1028	  # same prompt from scratch in a worktree that now holds the dead session's
  1029	  # partial, uncommitted edits is not a retry, it is a second worker on a dirty
  1030	  # tree.  review.sh already draws this line (ended-started < 15 s, tokens 0);
  1031	  # draw the same one here: retry only a death that did no work and left a clean
  1032	  # tree.  Anything else is left to the janitor's dead-session pass, which
  1033	  # re-dispatches under a per-(pr, role, head) budget with the state in hand.
  1034	  local dirty=""
  1035	  if [ "${WORKTREE_STATUS_AFTER_CODEX:-}" != "${WORKTREE_STATUS_BEFORE_CODEX:-}" ]; then
  1036	    dirty="${WORKTREE_STATUS_AFTER_CODEX:-}"
  1037	  fi
  1038	  [ "${DISPATCH_STATUS:-}" = refused ] || return 1
  1039	  [ "${DISPATCH_TURNS:-0}" = 0 ] || return 1
  1040	  case "${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL:-0}" in
  1041	    ''|0) ;;
  1042	    *) note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': the session used ${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL} tokens \
  1043	before dying, so a re-run would repeat work in a tree that holds its partial edits"
  1044	       return 1 ;;
  1045	  esac
  1046	  if [ -n "$dirty" ]; then
  1047	    note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': $WORKTREE_ABS has uncommitted changes from the \
  1048	dead session; the janitor's dead-session pass owns this one"
  1049	    return 1
  1050	  fi
  1051	  return 0
  1052	}

  1054	backoff_or_give_up() {
  1055	  # Jittered exponential backoff, base 30 s and cap 10 min. Returns 0 to retry.
  1056	  local exponent delay jitter total
  1057	  if [ "$ATTEMPT" -ge "$MAX_ATTEMPTS" ]; then
  1058	    note "attempt $ATTEMPT of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; no attempt left"
  1059	    return 1
  1060	  fi
  1061	  if cutoff_passed; then
  1062	    note "the run's dispatch cutoff has passed; not retrying after '$FAILURE_CLASS'"
  1063	    return 1
  1064	  fi
  1065	  exponent=$((ATTEMPT - 1))
  1066	  [ "$exponent" -le 20 ] || exponent=20
  1067	  delay=$((BACKOFF_BASE_S * (1 << exponent)))
  1068	  [ "$delay" -le "$BACKOFF_MAX_S" ] || delay="$BACKOFF_MAX_S"
  1069	  jitter=$((RANDOM % (delay / 2 + 1)))
  1070	  total=$((delay + jitter))
  1071	  ATTEMPT=$((ATTEMPT + 1))
  1072	  write_spool retrying
  1073	  note "attempt $((ATTEMPT - 1)) of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; \
  1074	retrying as attempt $ATTEMPT in ${total}s"
  1075	  sleep "$total"
  1076	  if cutoff_passed; then
  1077	    note "the run's dispatch cutoff passed during the backoff; stopping"
  1078	    return 1
  1079	  fi
  1080	  return 0
  1081	}

  1085	  # `refused` is not `failed`: the dispatch was never admitted, so it must not

    47	def health_state(root: Path, account: str) -> str:
    48	    """Endpoint health as ``capacity_controller.py`` last recorded it.
    49	
    50	    Absent, unreadable or unrecognized is ``up``: with no controller running the
    51	    router behaves exactly as it did before this field existed, and the cap

    63	def effective_caps(root: Path) -> list[int]:
    64	    """Per-account caps with a dead endpoint forced to zero.

    66	    Without this the router *prefers* the dead account: `choose_account` picks
    67	    the lower live/cap ratio, and an endpoint answering 503 keeps freeing slots

    70	    the cap to zero only ever narrows admission; it can never widen it.

    72	    caps = []

    82	def live_pids(directory: Path) -> set[int]:
    83	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    85	    for marker in directory.iterdir():

    88	        try:

    92	        except PermissionError:

   100	    """Share locked, malformed-row-tolerant history without discarding object metadata."""
   101	    rows = []
   102	    if registry.exists():
   103	        with registry.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
   104	            fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_SH)
   105	            for number, line in enumerate(handle, 1):
   106	                if not line.strip():
   107	                    continue
   108	                try:
   109	                    row = json.loads(line)
   110	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
   111	                    row = None
   112	                if not isinstance(row, dict):
   113	                    print(f"account routing: {registry}:{number}: "
   114	                          "skipping malformed registry record", file=sys.stderr)
   115	                    continue
   116	                rows.append(row)
   117	    return rows

   124	        for area in ("sessions", "archived_sessions"):

   126	                matches.add(account)

   206	def reserve(root: Path, requested: str, pid: int, wait: int, dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
   207	    """Reserve one worker slot under the lock shared by all dispatchers.
   208	
   209	    ``watchdog/drain`` is checked on every poll iteration, before the lock, and
   210	    raises `DrainRequested` so a queued dispatch releases itself during a pause
   211	    instead of being killed.  Absent file, absent health file: unchanged
   212	    behaviour in every respect.
   213	    """
   214	    if requested not in ('auto', *ACCOUNTS) or pid <= 0 or wait < 0:
   215	        raise ValueError('expected a valid account, positive pid and nonnegative wait')
   216	    accounts = root / "accounts"
   217	    accounts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   218	    deadline = time.monotonic() + wait
   219	    while True:
   220	        if (root / "watchdog" / "drain").exists():
   221	            raise DrainRequested('drain in progress; no reservation made')
   222	        with (accounts / "router.lock").open("a") as lock:
   223	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   224	            caps = effective_caps(root)
   225	            live = [len(live_pids(accounts / account)) for account in ACCOUNTS]
   226	            available = [account for index, account in enumerate(ACCOUNTS)
   227	                         if live[index] < caps[index] and requested in ('auto', account)]
   228	            if available:
   229	                selected = choose_account(live, caps) if len(available) == 2 else available[0]
   230	                if not dry_run:
   231	                    (accounts / selected / str(pid)).touch()
   232	                return selected
   233	            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
   234	            if dry_run or remaining <= 0:
   235	                raise CapacityExhausted('account capacity exhausted; no reservation made')
   236	        time.sleep(min(10, remaining))

  1023	def locked_append(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
  1024	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1025	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
  1026	    with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
  1027	        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
  1028	        try:
  1029	            handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1030	            if handle.tell():
  1031	                handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)
  1032	                if handle.read(1) != "\n":
  1033	                    handle.write("\n")
  1034	                handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1035	            handle.write(text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n")
  1036	            handle.flush()
  1037	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
  1038	        finally:
  1039	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

   320	def observe(rows: list[dict], name: str, endpoints: dict[str, str], roles: dict[str, str],
   321	            now: datetime, *, counter_window_s: int, fivexx_window_s: int) -> dict:
   322	    """Refusal and death counters for one account.
   323	
   324	    A ``failure_class`` the policy does not name — including the literal
   325	    ``unknown`` — is counted in neither direction, so a reworded provider message
   326	    leaves the cap where a hand-set cap would have been instead of collapsing it.
   327	    """

   329	                              "deaths_by_class": {}, "refusal_times": [], "fivexx_times": []}
   330	    counter_since = now - timedelta(seconds=counter_window_s)
   331	    fivexx_since = now - timedelta(seconds=fivexx_window_s)
   332	    for row in rows:
   333	        owner = next((endpoints[row[field]] for field in
   334	                      ("endpoint", "failure_endpoint", "account", "key_label")
   335	                      if isinstance(row.get(field), str) and row[field] in endpoints), None)
   336	        failure_class = row.get("failure_class")
   337	        if owner != name or not isinstance(failure_class, str) or not failure_class:
   338	            continue
   339	        if failure_class == "endpoint_5xx" and row["_ts"] >= fivexx_since:
   340	            bucket["fivexx_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   341	        if row["_ts"] < counter_since:
   342	            continue
   343	        role = roles.get(failure_class, "neutral")
   344	        if role == "refusal":
   345	            bucket["refusals"] += 1
   346	            bucket["refusal_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   347	        elif role == "death":

   350	                bucket["deaths_by_class"].get(failure_class, 0) + 1
   351	        else:
   352	            bucket["neutral"] += 1
   353	    bucket["refusal_times"].sort()
   354	    bucket["fivexx_times"].sort()

   526	def apply_aimd(account_state: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, live: int, now: datetime,

   528	    """Decrease first, so a refusal cannot be overtaken by an increase."""
   529	    notes: list[str] = []
   530	    aimd = knobs["aimd"]
   531	    window = timedelta(seconds=aimd["quiet_window_s"])
   532	    cap = int(account_state["cap"])
   533	    cursor = parse_ts(account_state.get("refusal_cursor"))
   534	    fresh = [moment for moment in counters["refusal_times"] if cursor is None or moment > cursor]
   535	    if fresh:
   536	        until = parse_ts(account_state.get("decrease_window_until"))
   537	        if until is None or now > until:
   538	            # The FIRST refusal of a window: step just under the concurrency that
   539	            # was refused.  ``live`` is sampled at the tick that observes it,
   540	            # which is the closest the controller gets to the moment of refusal —
   541	            # but when the refused sessions have already died it is 0 or 1, and a
   542	            # raw ``live - 1`` would collapse the cap to the floor and then climb
   543	            # back one slot per quiet window (an hour from 1 to 30 with the
   544	            # shipped defaults).  Fall back to what the account is KNOWN to have
   545	            # sustained before believing an instantaneous zero.
   546	            evidence = [value for value in
   547	                        (account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor"),
   548	                         account_state.get("measured_limit"))
   549	                        if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)]
   550	            basis = live if live > 1 else max([live] + evidence)
   551	            cap = max(floor, min(cap, basis - 1))
   552	            account_state["decrease_window_until"] = ts(now + window)
   553	            notes.append(f"decrease(first) live={live} basis={basis} -> {cap}")
   554	            observed = basis
   555	        else:
   556	            cap = max(floor, math.ceil(cap * float(aimd["decrease"])))
   557	            notes.append(f"decrease(x{aimd['decrease']}) -> {cap}")
   558	            observed = live
   559	        account_state.update(refusal_cursor=ts(max(fresh)), quiet_since=None)
   560	        if observed >= 1:  # a zero census is not evidence that one slot refused
   561	            seen = account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor")
   562	            account_state["observed_refusal_floor"] = (
   563	                observed if seen is None else min(int(seen), observed))
   564	    # ``live >= cap - 1`` keeps the cap honest: a cap nobody uses is not evidence
   565	    # of headroom.
   566	    if (not counters["refusals"] and not counters["deaths"]
   567	            and account_state["health"] == "up" and live >= cap - 1):

   632	            endpoints.setdefault(entry["label"], name)

   634	                   + [knobs_for(policy, name)["health"]["fivexx_window_s"] for name in accounts])
   635	    rows = read_session_rows(telemetry_dir() / "sessions.jsonl",
   636	                             now - timedelta(seconds=lookback))
   637	    live, waiters = count_live(accounts), count_waiters()

   639	                               "waiters": waiters, "accounts": {}}
   640	    caps: dict[str, int] = {}

   642

   644	        knobs = knobs_for(policy, name)
   645	        counters = observe(rows, name, endpoints, roles, now,
   646	                           counter_window_s=windows["counter_window_s"],
   647	                           fivexx_window_s=knobs["health"]["fivexx_window_s"])
   648	        account_state = state["accounts"].setdefault(name, new_account_state(name))
   649	        floor, ceiling = refresh(account_state, entry, knobs)
   650	        health = load_health(name, entry["endpoint"], now, knobs["health"]["probe_backoff_s"])

   653	        # and the disabled account in suppressing the probe, so a pause can never
   654	        # fire `codex exec` on the owner's keys after the deadline.

   656	                               no_probe=hold or paused or not entry["enabled"],

   658	                               probe_timeout_s=windows["probe_timeout_s"])

   665	            # the cap to 1 while state.json says paused (or while the brief says
   666	            # this key is off).  Pause outranks health in both directions.

   668	                notes.append("paused: cap 0" if paused else "disabled in the brief: cap 0")

   670	        elif action == "trip":

   672	            notes.append("endpoint down: cap 0")

   675	            # is the last thing to hand twenty sessions.

   677	                                 decrease_window_until=None, refusal_cursor=None)

   686	                           measured_hold_s=windows["measured_hold_s"])
   687	        if notes:
   688	            account_state["last_change"] = ts(now)
   689	        caps[name] = int(account_state["cap"])
   690	        measured = account_state["measured_limit"]
   691	        estimate["accounts"][name] = {
   692	            "nominal": entry["nominal_limit"], "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"],
   693	            "cap_now": caps[name], "live": live[name], "waiters": waiters,
   694	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m_by_class": counters["deaths_by_class"],
   695	            "measured_limit": measured,
   696	            "observed_refusal_floor": account_state["observed_refusal_floor"],
   697	            "external_inferred": (None if measured is None else entry["nominal_limit"]
   698	                                  - entry["external_reserved"] - int(measured)),

   729	def _append_jsonl(path: Path, record: dict) -> None:
   730	    """One locked, newline-safe append."""
   731	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   732	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
   733	    with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   734	        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   735	        try:
   736	            handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
   737	            if handle.tell():
   738	                handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)
   739	                if handle.read(1) != "\n":  # a previous writer died mid-line
   740	                    handle.write("\n")
   741	            handle.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
   742	            handle.flush()
   743	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
   744	        finally:
   745	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

   748	def append_stage(event: str, summary: dict, note: str) -> None:
   749	    """One ``capacity`` TRANSITION row in ``results/telemetry/stages.jsonl``.
   750	
   751	    Transitions only — ``init``, ``set``, ``pause``, ``resume``, and an endpoint
   752	    tripping or recovering.  The 60-second tick writes ``append_tick`` instead:
   753	    a row per tick would be ~1440 committed lines a day in a file that holds a
   754	    hundred for the whole project, and every one of them would ride into ``main``
   755	    on the merge daemon's telemetry batch.  The event names and the ``capacity``
   756	    stage are declared in ``local/protocols/meta.md`` (Telemetry duties).
   757	    """
   758	    if event not in STAGE_EVENTS:
   759	        raise ControllerError(
   760	            f"{event!r} is not a stages.jsonl transition for the capacity stage "
   761	            f"({', '.join(STAGE_EVENTS)}); per-tick records go to "
   762	            f"{capacity_dir() / 'ticks.jsonl'}")
   763	    record = {"ts": summary.get("ts") or ts(utcnow()), "stage": "capacity", "event": event,
   764	              "note": note, "capacity": summary}
   765	    _append_jsonl(telemetry_dir() / "stages.jsonl", record)

   768	def append_tick(summary: dict, note: str) -> Path:
   769	    """The per-tick record: runtime state under the cache root, never committed.
   770	
   771	    Trimmed to the last ``TICKS_KEEP`` rows by this writer, so nobody has to
   772	    prune it by hand and it cannot grow without bound on a long run.
   773	    """
   774	    path = capacity_dir() / "ticks.jsonl"
   775	    _append_jsonl(path, {"ts": summary.get("ts") or ts(utcnow()), "event": "tick",
   776	                         "note": note, "capacity": summary})
   777	    try:
   778	        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
   779	        if len(lines) > TICKS_KEEP:
   780	            tmp = path.with_suffix(".jsonl.tmp")
   781	            tmp.write_text("\n".join(lines[-TICKS_KEEP:]) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
   782	            os.replace(tmp, path)
   783	    except OSError:
   784	        pass  # a trim failure must never fail a control step
   785	    return path

   788	def render_note(summary: dict) -> str:
   789	    parts = [f"{name} {row['live']}/{row['cap']} {row['health']}"
   790	             + (" (" + "; ".join(row["notes"]) + ")" if row["notes"] else "")
   791	             for name, row in summary["accounts"].items()]
   792	    parts += ["hold"] if summary.get("hold") else []
   793	    parts += ["paused"] if summary.get("paused") else []
   794	    return "; ".join(parts) or "no accounts"

   800	def _lock(blocking: bool):
   801	    capacity_dir().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   802	    handle = (capacity_dir() / "controller.lock").open("a")
   803	    try:
   804	        fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX if blocking else fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   805	    except OSError:
   806	        handle.close()
   807	        return None
   808	    return handle

   811	def _require_lock(blocking: bool):
   812	    """``_lock`` or a named failure — never ``None`` reaching a ``.close()``.
   813	
   814	    ``flock`` can fail on a blocking wait too (EINTR is reachable), and an
   815	    unguarded ``lock.close()`` in a ``finally`` turns that into an
   816	    ``AttributeError`` traceback that ``main``'s handler does not catch.
   817	    """
   818	    handle = _lock(blocking)
   819	    if handle is None:
   820	        raise ControllerError(
   821	            f"cannot take {capacity_dir() / 'controller.lock'}; another capacity "
   822	            "controller holds it or the lock could not be acquired. Nothing was "
   823	            "written: the cap files are exactly as they were.")
   824	    return handle

   827	def _commit(state: dict, caps: dict[str, int], now: datetime, event: str, note: str,
   828	            dry_run: bool) -> int:
   829	    state["updated"] = ts(now)
   830	    if dry_run:
   831	        return sum(caps.values())
   832	    total = write_cap_files(caps)
   833	    _write_json(state_path(), state)
   834	    append_stage(event, {"ts": ts(now), "max_codex": total,
   835	                         "accounts": {name: {"cap": caps[name]} for name in caps}}, note)
   836	    return total

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""The apply -> pause -> resume round trip with the capacity controller present.
     3	
     4	`test_run_mode.py` runs against a stub repository root that carries the two
     5	committed templates and nothing else, so `run_mode.py` finds no capacity
     6	controller there and zeroes and restores the cap files itself.  That is a real
     7	configuration, but it is not the one a run uses, and the integration of the two
     8	tools had a defect only this configuration shows: with the controller installed
     9	but never seeded, `pause` asked it to save caps it had no state for, it saved
    10	zeros, and `resume` restored its floor -- a briefed 5/28/33 came back as 1/1/2
    11	while the resume message announced 5/28/33.  That is the 2026-09-12 failure the
    12	two tools exist to prevent, so it is pinned here.
    13	
    14	The repository root is a temporary directory whose ``local/bin`` is a symlink to
    15	the real one: the tools under test are the committed files, while every record
    16	they write (stages.jsonl, design-decisions.md) lands in the temporary tree.
    17	"""

    20	
    21	import json
    22	import os
    23	import shutil
    24	import subprocess
    25	import sys
    26	import tempfile
    27	import unittest

    30	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    31	BIN = REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin"
    32	RUN_MODE = BIN / "run_mode.py"
    33	CONTROLLER = BIN / "capacity_controller.py"
    34	POLICY = REPO_ROOT / "local" / "capacity-policy.json"

    39	class CapacityRoundTripTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    40	    def setUp(self) -> None:
    41	        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    42	        root = Path(self._tmp.name)
    43	        self.repo = root / "repo"
    44	        self.cache = root / "cache"
    45	        (self.repo / "local").mkdir(parents=True)
    46	        (self.repo / "results/telemetry/owner-tools").mkdir(parents=True)
    47	        (self.repo / "local" / "bin").symlink_to(BIN)
    48	        shutil.copy(POLICY, self.repo / "local" / "capacity-policy.json")
    49	        shutil.copy(TEMPLATE, self.repo / "results/telemetry/owner-tools"
    50	                    / "run-brief.template.json")
    51	        shutil.copy(SHIM, self.repo / "results/telemetry/owner-tools"
    52	                    / "owner-bin-codex")
    53	        self.watchdog = self.cache / "watchdog"
    54	        self.watchdog.mkdir(parents=True)
    55	        shutil.copy(TEMPLATE, self.watchdog / "run-brief.json")
    56	
    57	    def tearDown(self) -> None:
    58	        self._tmp.cleanup()

    62	    def run_mode(self, *argv: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    63	        env = dict(os.environ)
    64	        env["MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT"] = str(self.repo)
    65	        env["MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT"] = str(self.cache)
    66	        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(RUN_MODE), *argv],
    67	                              cwd=self.repo, env=env, capture_output=True,
    68	                              text=True)

    70	    def caps(self) -> dict[str, str]:
    71	        out = {}
    72	        for name in ("max-codex-primary", "max-codex-second", "max-codex"):

   682	sanitize_untrusted() {

    47	def health_state(root: Path, account: str) -> str:

    49

    63	def effective_caps(root: Path) -> list[int]:

     2	"""Push a branch and open (or adopt) its pull request on GitHub.
     3	
     4	Pre-0007 this wrote ``prs/<id>-<slug>/pr.md`` and never touched a remote.  GitHub
     5	now holds every field that record carried — head SHA, CI statuses bound to that
     6	SHA, the review verdict — leaving three jobs it does not do: branch hygiene
     7	(``check_bracket_free`` over ``FORBIDDEN_REF_CHARS`` plus ``git check-ref-format``;
     8	docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124 records that a ``]`` in a generated name once broke
     9	part of the parent's PR automation); refusing an empty diff instead of
    10	manufacturing a placeholder commit to make a PR openable; and create-or-adopt, so
    11	a second run adopts the head's unique open PR and PATCHes only the flags given
    12	(gh_common.py:194-200).  The push is real — hooks run, one ref is written, never
    13	``--all``, never a force.  Fail closed: a git or API failure exits 2 opening
    14	nothing.
    15	
    16	    pr_open.py --branch issue-42-pauli --issue 42 --title "feat(Quantum): ..." \
    17	               --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md --label formalization
    18	"""
